outcome: Application ↔ Oracle dependency direction is explicit and enforceable: Application owns WHAT context/schema is required, Oracle owns WHERE/HOW declared source data is read/adapted, and neither side leaks lifecycle or acceptance authority across the boundary.
currentProblem: Logical semantics are documented, but current colocation obscures the compile-time dependency direction. A package split without a precise semantic port can simply move the same coupling into circular imports or force Oracle to import application implementation internals.
constraints: Application remains authority for work-order/context schemas and required context selection.
Oracle owns source IO/adaptation only and must not claim work, schedule, accept, evaluate, recover or mutate product truth.
Prefer concrete Backend/QA ports earned by current use cases over a generic resolver abstraction.
Cross-package dependencies must be acyclic and testable.
Schema ownership may be shared only through a deliberately named contracts seam; Oracle must not depend on application orchestration implementation.
successCriteria: Research defines the exact semantic/compile-time port used by Backend and QA after physical extraction.
Dependency direction is acyclic and maps directly to documented authority: Application WHAT, Oracle WHERE/HOW.
Oracle can validate/assemble application-owned shapes without importing application orchestration runtime.
Negative cases prove Oracle cannot gain scheduling/acceptance/recovery/product-currentness authority.
Concrete ports remain sufficient for current repository/artifact sources; generic abstraction is explicitly deferred unless evidenced.
